On 30 July 2023, the SOCADEF, with rifles, abducted a truck driver in Konye (Meme, Sud-Ouest). They set his truck on fire. He was accused of distributing KADJI brewery products in Konye Subdivision without their permission.

On 13 July 2023, state security forces (coded as military) shot and killed a mentally ill civilian in Dadi (Manyu, Sud-Ouest) under unclear circumstances.

On 25 October 2023, military forces from the Rapid Intervention Battalion engaged in an armed confrontation with Ambazonian Separatists from the ADF in Korube (Momo, Nord-Ouest). On 10 March 2024, Ambazonian Separatists abducted a popular male petrol vendor at a local drinking spot on Ghana Street in Bamenda - Nkwen (Bamenda 3, Mezam, Nord-Ouest). The reason for his abduction is not known.
On 22 August 2021, military forces engaged in fire fight with Ambazonian separatists in Muea town, Buea subdivision (Fako, Sud-Ouest). No casualties reported.

On 28 March 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants ambushed and clashed with the military forces from the Rapid Intervention at the military outpost in Maloumri Abatchoua (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). Around 23 December 2022, suspected Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) fighters attacked Yegwa (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord) firing sporadically and entering civilian home. Casualties unknown. The military intervened and the fighters fled.
On 5 January 2021, kidney patients demonstrated at the regional hospital of Bamenda town (Mezam, Nord-Ouest), calling on the authorities to install new dialysis machines.

Around 20 May 2023 (as reported), Ambazonian Separatists killed a commercial motorbike rider whom they had abducted in Baba I (Ngo-Ketunjia, Nord-Ouest). On 15 November 2023, two unidentified groups of farmer and herders clashed in Biamo (Makary, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord). Casualties unknown.

On 11 August 2021, Musgum and Arab Choa ethnic militias clashed for the third day in a row, in Logone-Birni town (Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord) over a land dispute. No fatalities and/or casualties reported.

On 1 January 2021, the military forces attacked Mautu village (Buea, Fako, Sud-Ouest). No fatalities were reported. The military arrested 3 civilians who they suspected of being affiliated with the separatist fighters.

Around 16 May 2024 (as reported), Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants abducted 2 children in LdengLdeng (Mokolo, Mayo-Tsanaga, Extreme-Nord). The militants looted food items, livestock, clothing and household items.
On 4 August 2022, suspected Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) attacked civilians in their home in Bonderi (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord) killing 2 civilians. Their throats were slit by the assailants.

On 28 August 2022, Ambazonian separatists fired several shots at a military checkpoint and engaged the soldiers in an armed clash in Eyumodjock subdivision, coded to Eyumojock (Manyu, Sud-Ouest). No casualties were recorded.
Around 21 August 2020 (between 21 - 22 August), Boko Haram attacked Katoua village (Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord), taking away motorbikes, clothes and livestock.

On 28 March 2023, Ambazonian Separatists attacked construction workers on the road between Njikwa and Ngie Subdivisions, coded to Njikwa (Mbengwi, Momo, Nord-Ouest). In a video the separatists claim that the only development they want is for 'La Republique' to leave their land.

On 19 November 2022, Ambazonian Separatists abducted two bike riders at a checkpoint in Ekombe Bonji (Meme, Sud-Ouest). Property destruction: On 30 November 2021, suspected Ambazonian separatists burnt a portion of the market stores belonging to Mbounda people in Nkwen village, Bamenda 3 subdivision (Bamenda - Nkwen, Mezam, Nord-Ouest).

On 10 September 2023, Ambazonian Separatists from SOCADEF engaged in an armed confrontation with state security forces (coded as military) along the Kumba - Mamfe road in Ikiliwindi Mile 10 (Meme, Sud-Ouest) after the Separatists shot at a truck transporting cocoa which was being escorted by the military forces. Movement of forces: Around 5 October 2023, Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants were seen regrouping in the abandoned village of Tamballam, 24 kilometers from Kolofata (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord) close to the border of Nigeria.
On 5 April 2020, Boko Haram attacked the village of Ngossi, in Mokolo subdivision (Mayo-Tsanaga, Extreme-Nord), killing 3 people.

On 1 December 2022, Ambazonian Separatists abducted some students from their private student hostel in Bambili (Mezam, Nord-Ouest). The circumstances leading to their abduction is not known.

On 19 August 2024, the military forces from the Rapid Intervention clashed with the ISWAP or Boko Haram militants in Yabogo (Mora, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord) during an army patrol. There were no fatalities on the military side, militant casualties unknown. 2 soldiers were injured and evacuated to Salak. The military forces carried out a sweep of the area without success.

On 3 September 2023, the military forces (Rapid Intervention) ambushed Boko Haram militants [JAS faction] in Walassa (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). Casualties unknown. 4 militants were arrested, 2 weapons and other military equipment and a herd of oxen were recovered.
Around 2 May 2024 (as reported), Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants attacked and killed a trainee Christian pastor in Tourou (Mokolo, Mayo-Tsanaga, Extreme-Nord) during an attack.

On 2 June 2023, suspected Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants attacked a man at his farm in Greya (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). He was killed in the attack. He had gone to search for firewood when he was attacked.

On 13 February 2023, Ambazonian Separatists fired several gunshots in Ekok (Manyu, Sud-Ouest). Two male civilians were injured while two others were abducted and taken to their hideout. On 24 June 2022, suspected Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) attacked a private residential area in Mtseukar (Mayo-Tsanaga, Extreme-Nord) wounding 2 civilians. They also looted food items, small livestock and valuables.

On 10 July 2023, Ambazonian Separatists physically assaulted villagers in Zoa (Menchum, Nord-Ouest) and demanded them to finance their activities. No information on injuries.

On 20 May 2023, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces detonated an IED against a state security forces team (coded as military) along the Kumba - Mbonge road in Lipenja Village (Ndian, Sud-Ouest), leading to an armed confrontation. On 6 August 2023, state security forces (coded as military) injured a child with a stray bullet in Kouki (Bui, Nord-Ouest) when they fired gunshots indiscriminately while approaching an unmanned Ambazonian Separatist vehicular checkpoint. He was taken to the hospital for treatment.

The militants also temporary abducted one other civilian but released him later.
On 30 May 2020, Ambazonian separatists captured and severely beat up a humanitarian worker before releasing him the following day, in the Nord-Ouest region (Mezam, Nord-Ouest).

On 2 April 2024, ISWAP or Boko Haram militants abducted 4 fishers from a fishing area in Darak (Darak, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord) for an unknown reason.
On 3 December 2023, Ambazonian Separatists intercepted a truck and kidnapped the driver and his assistant in Nkwen (Bamenda - Nkwen, Bamenda 3, Mezam, Nord-Ouest).

On 30 August 2022, ISWAP or Boko Haram fighters clashed with the Cameroonian military forces in Amtchoukouli, near Fotokol (Fotokol, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord) leading to the injury of 1 civilian. The civilian was hit by a stray bullet. He was taken to the hospital for treatment.

On 29 March 2022, suspected Ambazonian Separatist fighters abducted the head of the Wabane intergrated health centre in Magha, coded to Menji (Wabane, Lebialem, Sud-Ouest). The separatists demanded a ransom fee for his release.

On 8 May 2020, Boko Haram raided several houses in Kerawa village, Kolofata subdivision (Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord), taking away clothes, foods, and motorcycles.

On 9 February 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from the SOCADEF faction clashed with the security forces, coded as the military forces in Ikiliwindi Mile 12 (Kumba 2, Meme, Sud-Ouest). 1 Separatist, 1 soldier and 3 civilians were killed. The Separatists had fired at 2 public vehicles when the military forces intervened.
Looting: On 14 October 2024, suspected Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants looted 2 motorbikes from ethnic Arab Choa in Ganse (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord).

Movement of forces: On 31 July 2024, an unidentified armed group suspected of being ISWAP or Boko Haram militants was seen in the bushes of Maloumri Abatchoua (Malloumri) (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord).
On 25 July 2020, Boko Haram attacked the village of Zelevet, Mokolo subdivision (Mayo-Tsanaga, Extreme-Nord), killing one person.

On 31 May 2024, Ambazonian Separatists abducted a civilian from her private residence in Center Bolt in Bamenda - Nkwen (Bamenda 3, Mezam, Nord-Ouest). The Separatists also fired shots in the air without causing casualties.

On 21 August 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from the ADF faction attacked and injured a traditional ruler at his private residence in Ayukaba (Mamfe, Manyu, Sud-Ouest) for an unknown reason. The Separatists attempted to abduct another traditional ruler but he escaped. The Separatists looted money and valuables from both traditional rulers.

On 19 April 2023, state security forces (coded as military) engaged in an armed confrontation with Ambazonian Separatists in Bamenda - Mankon (Mezam, Nord-Ouest). 4 Separatists were killed, and one soldier was severely wounded. Some ammunition was recovered.

On 6 March 2020, unidentified individuals armed with machetes and bows attacked the fishermen village of Willy, near Afade in Makary subdivision (Logone-Et-Chari, Extreme-Nord). They took away clothes and cell phones. No fatality and/or casualty reported.

Other: On 3 July 2023, state security forces, coded as military, fired into air several gunshots in Kakar (Ndu, Donga-Mantung, Nord-Ouest). The event was preceded by the armed clash between the military and Ambazonian Separatists a day before this event (coded separately).

On 22 September 2020, hundreds of supporters of the MRC (opposition) party demonstrated in several neighbourhoods of Douala city (Wouri, Littoral) to demand the departure of president Paul Biya. The military forces fired tear gas to disperse them. One demonstrator was reportedly killed, several injured, and 31 arrested. The MRC says 'several' were killed in those demonstrations throughout the Littoral region.

On 1 February 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants armed with rifles killed one male civilian and injured five civilians in Guedjele (Koza, Mayo-Tsanaga, Extreme-Nord). The attackers also looted foodstuffs, small farm animals, bicycles and valuables from civilians.

On 13 September 2024, the military forces clashed and repelled an attack from the Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants in Homaka (Mora, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). After the clashes, the military forces discovered blood on the ground indicating either injuries or deaths. Casualties unknown.
On 12 May 2024, Ambazonian Separatists abducted two men from their private residence in Banga Bakundu (Kumba 3, Meme, Sud-Ouest). The militants accused them of collaborating with government forces.
Looting: On 14 July 2023, Ambazonian Separatists stopped an unspecified number of vehicles and extorted money from passengers on their way to Guzang market in Guzan (Momo, Nord-Ouest).

On 14 June 2022, (between 12 - 16 June), Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) attacked Ndrok, near Tourou (Mokolo, Mayo-Tsanaga, Extreme-Nord) killing 3 civilians, all heads of families. Vigilance committee in the village were unable to prevent the attack due to limited materials and weapons.

Looting: On 19 January 2023, Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) fighters looted Matakaya (Mora, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord) stealing food items from a field. The Cameroonian military forces followed the fighters and recovered the stolen goods. There were no clashes.
Looting: On 26 January 2021, Boko Haram fighters looted Ganse village (Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord), taking away 50 sheep and other goods. No fatality and/or casualty reported.

On 22 May 2022, unidentified armed group attacked Christian civilians at a church in Kajifu (Akwaya, Manyu, Sud-Ouest) leading to unknown number of fatalities. Several were also injured. The assailants also destroyed identification documents, especially those with Cameroonian nationality.
Property destruction: On 18 January 2021, Ambazonian separatists burnt a vehicle down in Buea town (Fako, Sud-Ouest), for not respecting the ghost town.
On 7 April 2020, Boko Haram attacked the village of Toufou 1, in Tourou subdivision (Mayo-Tsanaga, Extreme-Nord). They killed one person and destroyed houses and a health centre.

On 3 June 2023, state security forces (coded as military) physically assaulted around five male civilians at their farms in Wanangwen neighborhood in Wum (Menchum, Nord-Ouest). They were suspected of being Ambazonian Separatists. No information on injuries.

Other: On 6 May 2024, Ambazonian Separatists fired several warning shots in the air and blocked different road segment in Bamenda (Bamenda II, Mezam, Nord-Ouest). Their actions were to reinforce their Monday lockdown.

On 27 November 2023, an unidentified armed group armed with machetes attacked a civilian at Hile-Hausa neighborhood in Kousseri (Kousseri, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord) in an attempt to steal his motorbike. The victim was injured and he was able to escape with his motorbike.
Looting: On 24 July 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants looted 1 motorcycle and small farm animals from civilians in Ndaba (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord).
On 28 January 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants attacked and injured a pastoralist in Assighassia (Mayo-Moskota, Mayo-Tsanaga, Extreme-Nord) during a cattle raid.

On 15 April 2024, ISWAP or Boko Haram militants attacked the MNJTF post in Zigue (Logone-Birni, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord). At least 1 soldier was killed and another soldier is missing, the militants stole and set fire to a military vehicle, dismantled weapons and stole ammunition. The casualties on the militant side are unknown and 1 militant was arrested.

On 29 August 2024, security forces, coded as the military forces, arrested 25 men and 4 women from their private residences in Banga Ngonge, Mbonge commune (Mbonge, Meme, Sud-Ouest) during a search operation to dislodge Ambazonian Separatists from their hideouts.

On 18 January 2021, state forces arrested dozens of youth in Bamiyan in Ndop subdivision (coded to Ndop), when they went on an arresting spree, arresting anyone with any links to fighters in armed groups (likely Ambazonian separatists).

Looting: On 9 August 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from the ADF faction forcibly collected 2,000 Franc CFA from commercial drivers and 1,000 Franc CFA from their passengers at an illegal checkpoint mounted by the Separatists in Numba (Mamfe, Manyu, Sud-Ouest).

On 24 August 2024, gendarmerie forces shot and killed 1 Ambazonian Separatist along a secondary road in Bambui (Tubah, Mezam, Nord-Ouest). The gendarmerie forces took the body and displayed it at the road junction in Bambui.

On 19 November 2020, hundreds of members of the Cameroon association to improve hygiene demonstrated in Douala city (Wouri, Littoral) to mark the World Toilet Day and to call on the authorities to provide more public bathrooms.

Other: On 4 July 2024, Ambazonian Separatists riding on motorbikes fired sporadic gunshots into the air as they passed through the crossroads of Chamkfung-Djottin, coded to Djottin (Noni, Bui, Nord-Ouest). The reason for the gunshots is unknown.
On 4 February 2022, Ambazonian separatists engaged military forces in an armed clash around Banja (Bamenda - Nkwen, Bamenda 3, Mezam, Nord-Ouest) There were no reported casualties.

On 12 December 2022, Microbes Youth Militia stormed the Laquintinie Hospital in Douala (Douala 1, Wouri, Littoral) leading to several injured. The youths attacked the hospital after the police killed their members (coded as a separate event).
On 23 June 2022, military forces shot and killed two male civilians in Ekombe Bonji (Kumba 1, Meme, Sud-Ouest).

Non-violent activity: On 16 July 2022, Gendarmes from the Jakiri Brigade collected more than 60 ID cards in Jakiri town (Jakiri, Bui, Nord-Ouest) and asked civilians to pay 10,000Frs to have their ID cards returned.

Looting: On 6 September 2023, Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants looted travelling civilians along the Goudegou-Amchide road, coded to Amchide (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). The militants stole motorbikes and goods.
On 7 February 2021, suspected Ambazonian Separatists attacked a truck transporting beer in Baba I (Ngo-Ketunjia, Nord-Ouest). They abducted the driver and his assistant.
On 30 October 2020, Boko Haram nightly attacked Tchokoyaba village, Mora subdivision (Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord), killing one person and severely injuring 2 others. They also took away sheep and money.

On 4 September 2023, Ambazonian Separatists from Bui, Ndu, and Nwa attacked a Gendarmerie station in Lus (Donga-Mantung, Nord-Ouest). The Separatists took control of the station, and civilians fled the village. Casualties unknown.
Looting: On 8 October 2023, Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants looted civilians on their way to their field in Bourvare (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). 2 motorbikes were stolen.
On 4 December 2023, Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants abducted a young girl from her farm in Zamga (Mayo-Moskota, Mayo-Tsanaga, Extreme-Nord).
Looting: On 18 October 2021, Boko Haram fighters attacked Kerawa village, Kolofata subdivision (Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord), taking away 84 cattle heads.
On 2 April 2024, commercial bike riders protested in Kumba (Kumba 1, Meme, Sud-Ouest) against insecurity and the killing of their colleagues by Ambazonian Separatists.

On 25 September 2021, the military forces engaged in fire fights with Ambazonian separatists in Kumbo town (Bui, Nord-Ouest). A military transport truck also hit an IED planted by suspected Ambazonian separatists in Kumbo town, resulting in a soldier being killed and about a dozen others severely injured.

Property destruction: On 22 July 2024, the security forces, coded as the military forces set some 6 civilian shops on fire along a secondary road in Njikfuin in the Belo Commune (Tubah, Mezam, Nord-Ouest) for an unknown reason during a military operation to dislodge Separatists from their hideouts.

On 23 July 2024, Cameroonian soldiers clashed with Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants after an incursion in Maloumri (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). The militants chased the farmers in their fields before the soldiers in the area deployed and repelled them. There were no casualties.

On 3 June 2024, Mafa tribe and Zoulgo tribe clashed in Roua (Soulede-Roua, Mayo-Tsanaga, Extreme-Nord) over dispute on land. There were no fatalities. 14 people were injured, including 4 seriously. 57 huts were burnt with fuel from motorbikes. Food items were also destroyed and some livestock stolen.

On 22 May 2022, suspected Ambazonian separatists abducted 10 civilians along Bamenda-Ekok road, coded to Bamenda (Bamenda 1, Mezam, Nord-Ouest) demanding a ransom fee of 3 million central African CFA (XAF).

On 11 September 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants abducted a civilian with oxen between Bourvare and Kolofata, coded to Bourvare (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). The militants looted oxen.

On 28 May 2021, a group of Mbororo herders attacked a group of local farmers with their machetes in Gor village, Madingring subdivision (Mayo-Rey, Nord) following a dispute over their grazing area, killing 2 of them. Another group of villagers later backed up the farmers alongside soldiers patrolling in the area. They also clashed with the Mbororo, resulting in one of them killed (total of 3 fatalities).

On 24 September 2022, suspected Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) clashed with police and members of the vigilance group at a checkpoint in Kolofata (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord) leading to the death of 1 police officer and 1 vigilance member. Their weapons and a motorbike were stolen.

On 12 December 2022, Ambazonian Separatists rounded up traders at gun point and kidnapped them at a market in Tinto (Manyu, Sud-Ouest), moving them to their hideout under unclear circumstances. They were released few hours later after paying an unspecified amount of money to the Separatists.
On 11 February 2024, military forces clashed with Ambazonian Separatists in Mbonge (Mbonge, Meme, Sud-Ouest). There were 2 fatalities.
Looting: On 25 June 2023, Ambazonian Separatists seized a phone and money from a lawyer in Njirong (Donga-Mantung, Nord-Ouest). It is unknown why he was targeted.

On 5 October 2024, the security forces (coded as the military forces) were accused of killing a suspected former Ambazonian Separatist in the Mile 17 neighborhood in Buea (Buea, Fako, Sud-Ouest) for an unknown reason after the suspect was arrested and taken to a detention facility.
On 1 July 2021, Ambazonian separatists shot and killed a school administrator in Up Station neighborhood of Kumba town, Ekondo Titi subdivision (Ndian, Sud-Ouest).

Around 4 March 2024 (as reported), suspected Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants clashed with a suspected unidentified armed group in the Guederou Bush in Guederou (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). Members of the military forces and the self-defence militia on patrol discovered 2 decomposed bodies. The exact circumstances of their death are not known
On 13 February 2024, an unidentified armed group in an unknown uniform abducted a shopkeeper in front of the Zenith Hotel in Kousseri (Kousseri, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord).

On 10 June 2022, Ambazonian Separatists killed a gendarmerie officer in Matuke, near Mbanga (Mbanga, Moungo, Littoral). The officer was on his way to Pendamboko when he was ambushed by the separatists.

On 17 November 2021, the police forces tortured one suspect under their custody in Douala city, Douala 1 subdivision (Wouri, Littoral). The victim was arrested after a private dispute with a police officer. He later died of his wounds. Three police officers were later arrested in connection to that incident.
On 5 December 2020, an IED planted by suspected Ambazonian separatists detonated in Matezen village, Santa subdivision (Mezam, Nord-Ouest), injuring three people.

On 17 June 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction attacked and clashed with the Gendarmerie patrol unit along a secondary road in Nganjo Bolende (Mbonge, Meme, Sud-Ouest). 2 gendarmerie officers were killed and a stray bullet killed a civilian.
On 20 May 2024, security forces members, coded as military forces, exchanged fire with Ambazonian Separatists in Manja (Mundemba, Ndian, Sud-Ouest). 1 Separatist militant was killed.

On 22 April 2024, Ambazonian Separatists attacked Kuk (Wum, Menchum, Nord-Ouest). The Separatists abducted 2 civilians and set fire to the private residence of a parliament member. There were no fatalities. No information on the injuries. The abductees were released after a ransom was paid.

Looting: On 24 September 2024, ISWAP or Boko Haram militants looted livestock from the foot of Mount Greya (Greya) (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). Some of the animals later return to the village but 15 remain missing.

On 28 March 2024, the military forces from the Rapid Intervention clashed and repelled an attack from Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants in Maloumri (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). Casualties unknown. No information on the injuries.
Around 21 September 2020 (as reported), residents captured and beat up one person in Bamenda town (Mezam, Nord-Ouest) for allegedly attempting to steal a five-year old child.

On 13 December 2022, microbes youth militia attacked several neighborhoods of Douala (Douala 1, Wouri, Littoral). Casualties unknown. Several have been injured. The attackers carried sharp objects including knives, cutlasses and razor blades to attack civilians and looted them. The attack left many civilians stranded in shops and homes.
Other: On 25 December 2023, the military forces fired several gunshots after suspecting the presence of Ambazonian Separatists in Kikaikiliki (Kumbo, Bui, Nord-Ouest).

On 8 March 2023, Ambazonian Separatists detonated a road planted IED targeted at state security forces, coded as military forces as they were transiting in a vehicle along Mbengwi road, coded to Mbengwi (Momo, Nord-Ouest). There were no casualties.

Other: On 26 September 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from the ADF faction riding on motorbikes forcefully entered the premises of a primary school in Bambui (Tubah, Mezam, Nord-Ouest). The Separatists ordered the school to close until 22 October 2024, and students were sent back to their homes.
On 8 June 2022, military forces killed two Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces in Bakossi, near Kumba (Meme, Sud-Ouest) including a high-profile ARF operative.

On 31 July 2023, ISWAP or Boko Haram militants attacked Darak (Darak, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord). Since their arrival, the militants looted and killed civilians, resulting in the discovery of 12 corpses by villagers. 4 unspecified casualties split across 2 events. Fatalities coded as 2. The militants had come to collect taxes from the fishermen.

Displacement: On 2 February 2023, civilians were displaced for fear of retaliation attacks from, the state security forces in Diongo (Dibombari, Moungo, Littoral) after suspected Ambazonian Separatists mounted an illegal checkpoint paralyzing vehicle movement.
On 3 September 2024, Ambazonian Separatists abducted a civilian from his private residence in Bambui (Tubah, Mezam, Nord-Ouest) for an unknown reason.
On 5 February 2024, the Ambazonian Restoration Forces kidnapped two employees of the Cameroon Development Cooperation (CDC) at a palm plantation in Sanje (West-Coast, Fako, Sud-Ouest).

On 1 July 2022, Ambazonian Separatists (Red Dragons Faction) attacked a market in Piah, coded to Dschang (Dschang, Menoua, Ouest). The separatists shot sporadically creating a stampede, burnt vehicles and looted shops. Several were injured, the event did not lead to fatalities.

On 20 March 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction clashed with the military forces from the Rapid Intervention in Bombe Bakundu (Kumba 3, Meme, Sud-Ouest) during an operation to dislodge Separatists hideouts. 1 Separatist was killed. The military forces recovered a weapon.

Property destruction: On 25 November 2023, the army's Rapid Intervention Battalion fired warning gunshots in the air and destroyed a vehicle at the market square in Bamessi (Babessi, Ngo-Ketunjia, Nord-Ouest).
On 28 December 2020, the Central African RRR armed group kidnapped 3 gendarmes in Ngaoui village (Mbere, Adamaoua), near the border with CAR.

On 23 September 2021, supporters of the CPDM (ruling) party attacked and burnt down the house of the subprefect of Bengbis town (Dja-et-Lobo, Sud). They accused him of interfering in the election of the heads of the local CPDM section.

Around 7 August 2023, Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants clashed with the self-defense militia (COVI) in Bakarise, near Kerawa (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). 3 civilians were killed and 1 woman was injured. 1 militant was also killed.

Other: On 8 August 2024, police forces cordoned off and searched civilian residents during an operation to dislodge Ambazonian Separatists from their hideouts at Nitop 4 and 5 neighborhoods in Bamenda - Mankon (Bamenda 2, Mezam, Nord-Ouest). During the operation, the police forces broke doors and forcefully entered civilian homes. There were no fatalties or injuries.
Looting: On 13 November 2023, Boko Haram militants [JAS faction] looted civilians in Guederou (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord) and forced them to flee before stealing 2 motorbikes.

Around 21 April 2024 (as reported), Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants clashed with the military forces in Kolofata (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). Casualties unknown. No information on the injuries. The militants looted several nearby villages.
Looting: On 17 August 2024, ISWAP or Boko Haram militants looted food items, clothing, household goods, sleeping equipment and livestock in Waraga (Mora, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord).

On 4 January 2024, the Ambazonian Restoration Forces ambushed a military patrol unit in Munyenge (Muyuka, Fako, Sud-Ouest). During the resulting gun battle, they shot and killed three military members.
On 6 March 2023, Ambazonian Separatists engaged in an armed confrontation with security forces (coded as military) in Bambui (Mezam, Nord-Ouest). No casualties.

On 13 December 2023, the Ambazonian Restoration Forces attacked civilians at a drinking spot in Lobange (Konye, Meme, Sud-Ouest). They fired multiple gunshots, physically assaulted an unspecified number of civilians, and kidnapped the owner of the drinking spot. The accused the civilians of defying their orders to close the drinking spot, as the owner refused to pay the Ambazonian Restoration Forces -imposed levies on all businesses in the subdivision. No information on injuries.

On 10 August 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from the ADF faction attacked and injured a civilian in Bessi (Babessi, Ngo-Ketunjia, Nord-Ouest) when the Separatists tried to take the motorbike from its owner. The civilian was injured, and the motorbike was damaged.

On 25 June 2024, the security forces, coded as the military forces, clashed with the Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction at an army checkpoint in Tole (Buea, Fako, Sud-Ouest). There were no fatalities. The military forces recovered weapons the Separatists left behind.

On 13 October 2022, suspected ISWAP or Boko Haram fighters tried to abduct civilians in Dore-Liman, coded to Hile Alifa (Hile-Alifa, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord) but were warned of their arrival by the lookouts causing civilians to flee to Bagaram village.

On 30 September 2022, Ambazonian Separatists ambushed military forces in Melim (Bui, Nord-Ouest) after they attempted to take down the 'Ambazonian independence flag' which had been hoisted by the fighters on the eve of 1 October. Casualties unknown.
On 5 May 2024, a suspected grenade exploded in Kerawa (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord) when children were collecting scrap metal. A man and his child were killed. Total 2 fatalities.

Around 8 November 2023, Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants clashed with the military forces in Tchakamari, coded to Mora (Mora, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). 1 soldier was killed and 2 wounded. The military camp was burnt down and weapons and ammunition stolen.

On 23 June 2022, Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) clashed with an unidentified armed group as their attempted to attack Nguetchewe (Mayo-Moskota, Mayo-Tsanaga, Extreme-Nord) leading to the killing of 1 Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) fighter and several wounded. 2 civilians were also slightly wounded and taken to the hospital for treatment.

On 21 January 2020, a group of dismissed staff representatives of the Douala city council (Wouri, Littoral) protested to demand the payment of indemnities and unpaid salaries due before their dismissal.
On 11 November 2023, the army's Rapid Intervention Battalion shot dead an aged man in Batibo (Batibo, Momo, Nord-Ouest).

On 27 August 2024, ISWAP or Boko Haram militants ambushed and clashed with the self-defense militia in Ldagam (Koza, Mayo-Tsanaga, Extreme-Nord). There were no fatalities. 3 self-defense militia and 1 civilian assisting the self-defense militia were wounded. The injured were treated at the Koza Adventist Hospital.

Looting: On 8 September 2023, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction led by 'General Omega' extorted from a contractor the sum of 1.5 million FCFA (approximately USD 2.5k) to allow him to carry out construction works in Ngali (Manyu, Sud-Ouest). They also intercepted and extorted 20,000 FCFA (approximately USD 33) from a truck driver transporting industrial material from Nigeria to the project site.

On 24 July 2023, state security forces (coded as military) ambushed Ambazonian Separatists from SOCADEF at a vehicular checkpoint along the Kumba - Mamfe road in Kurume (Meme, Sud-Ouest). One Separatist was killed, and an unknown number of Separatists were injured.
On 31 July 2023, state security forces (coded as military) killed four Ambazonian Separatists, including 'Commander John,' at their hideout in Abuh (Menchum, Nord-Ouest).

On 30 April 2024, suspected ISWAP or Boko Haram militants attacked and killed 1 civilian working as a CFA/NAIRA money exchanger in Hile Ndougoul, coded to Amchilga (Makary, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord). The militants looted money.
On 28 March 2022, suspected Ambazonian Separatists attacked the village of Magha (Lebialem, Sud-Ouest). They killed a teacher and abducted 5 civilians.

On 5 February 2023, military forces of Cameroon on an operation to track Ambazonian Separatists at their hideout engaged some separatists fighters who set up a roadside ambush in an armed clash at Baba I (Babessi, Ngo-Ketunjia, Nord-Ouest). The separatists detonated IEDs that destroyed three armored vehicles of the troops, the clash lasted four nearly 4 hours; 4 soldiers were killed, an unspecified were wounded and ammunition was seized by the separatists, 5 separatists were also killed.
On 19 October 2021, tens of women and girls dressed in black demonstrated in Mankon village, Bamenda 2 subdivision (Bamenda - Mankon, Mezam, Nord-Ouest) against rape and sexual violence.

On 15 July 2023, state security forces, coded as military, shot and killed 6 men and arrested 2 women civilians in their house in Awing quarter in Mankon (Bamenda - Mankon, Mezamn, Nord-Ouest) due to unspecified intelligence.

On 31 July 2023, Boko Haram militants [JAS faction] clashed with the security forces between Djibrili and Zamga (Mayo-Moskota, Mayo-Tsanaga, Extreme-Nord) located next to each other. 1 woman was injured while her infant child was killed. The militants stole livestock, food and fertilizer.
On 10 February 2022, assumed Ambazonian separatists beat an NGO worker with sticks in Buea locality (Buea, Fako, Sud-Ouest) and abducted him, claiming that he did not respect the lockdown decision.
On 11 September 2023, Ambazonian Separatists from SOCADEF ambushed state security forces (coded as military) along the Kumba - Mamfe road in Ikiliwindi Mile 10 (Meme, Sud-Ouest). No casualties.
Looting: On 30 September 2022, Ambazonian Separatists extorted an unspecified amount of money from drivers and some traders transporting illicit fuel at a checkpoint in Ashum (Manyu, Sud-Ouest).

On 4 October 2022, Cameroonian military forces (Rapid Intervention) clashed with Boko Haram (JAS) in Djakana neighborhood in Limani (Mora, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord) leading to unknown fatalities or injuries. The assailants tried to enter Limani but were pushed back by the military.

On 24 August 2024, after receiving a tip-off, the military forces from the Rapid Intervention ambushed and clashed with Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction at the Separatist hideout Owe (Muyuka, Fako, Sud-Ouest). 5 Separatists were killed.

On 8 December 2023, Ambazonian Separatists shot and killed a civilian in Baba I (Babessi, Ngo-Ketunjia, Nord-Ouest).They accused the victim of impersonating separatists and extorting money and valuables from civilians.

On 20 May 2023, Ambazonian Separatists engaged in an armed confrontation with state security forces (coded as military) in Atoini (Boyo, Nord-Ouest) to disrupt celebrations of the National Day. No casualties.

On 11 September 2022, military forces arrived at a checkpoint manned by Ambazonia Separatists from the Bafut 7 Karta faction and killed one fighter at Agyati in Bafut subdivision, coded to Bafut (Mezam, Nord-Ouest).

On 10 August 2021, Musgum and Arab Choa ethnic militias clashed for the second day in a row, in Logone-Birni town (Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord) over a land dispute. 12 people were killed and around 48 others injured, and more than 100 houses burnt down.

Weapons seizure: Around 2 February 2023, the national gendarmerie in a special operation seized weapons and ammunition in Gonna, coded to Garoua (Garoua 2, Benoue, Nord). The operation began on 22 January 2023 to arrest criminals who have been attacking and abducting civilians in the area.
On 21 May 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from Bui Unity Warriors faction attacked security forces members, coded as military forces, in Jakiri (Jakiri, Bui, Nord-Ouest). No casualties.

On 19 April 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants attacked civilians along the Kouyape - Bornori road, coded to Kouyape (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). Casualties unknown. No information on the injuries.

On 26 June 2022, the Cameroonian Military forces (Rapid Intervention) clashed with suspected Ambazonian separatists in Yelum, coded to Nseh (Nkum, Bui, Nord-Ouest) leading to the death of at least 5. The military arrested at least 7 civilians claiming they knew the whereabouts of the separatists.

On 15 October 2023, members of the same Shuwa Arab community clashed in Hilele (Goulfey, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord). There were no fatalities, 1 person was injured and a bean field destroyed.

Property destruction: On 2 July 2023, Ambazonian Separatists fired several gunshots in the air, intercepted and held a bike rider by the road and burned his bike at unspecified place in Bamenda 3, coded to Nkwen (Bamenda - Nkwen, Mezam, Nord-Ouest). There is no further information available.

On 18 October 2024, Ambazonian Separatists abducted a former government official and his wife from their private residence in an unknown location in the Ndu commune (Ndu, Donga-Mantung, Nord-Ouest). The former government official was released a few hours later, but his wife remained with the Separatists. The Separatists accused the wife of being a school teacher and demanded a ransom for her release.
Around 15 July 2020 (month of), Ambazonian separatists killed a village quarter head in Balikumbat town (Ngo-Ketunjia, Nord-Ouest).

On 21 November 2022, military forces raided Pinyin (Santa, Mezam, Nord-Ouest) to dislodge armed fighters (likely Ambazonian Separatists) and to capture a former fighter who escaped after surrendering and who had previously assisted the military forces in locating the Separatists hideout. The soldiers fired a few shots in the air and then arrested approximately 53 civilians, interrogated them, and then released them all. No casualties were recorded.
Looting: On 21 July 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction looted 2 million Franc CFA from a businesswoman around Ekona Yard (Muyuka, Fako, Sud-Ouest).
On 1 August 2020, the military forces shot and killed an Ambazonian separatist commander in Babessi town (Ngo-ketunjia, Sud-Ouest).
On 1 February 2021, military forces undertook an operation in Owe (Muyuka, Fako, Sud-Ouest). They arrested four civilians.

On 8 August 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from the ADF faction ambushed and clashed with security forces, coded as the military forces, at an illegal checkpoint in Jikijem (Oku, Bui, Nord-Ouest). 1 traveling civilian was hit and killed by a stray bullet.

On 11 January 2024, a customs officer opened fire at a transiting commercial transport vehicle at a vehicle checkpoint along Kumba - Mamfe road axis in Okoyong (Mamfe, Manyu, Sud-Ouest). A pedestrian woman was hit and killed by a stray bullet.

On 13 August 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from the SOCADEF faction abducted 2 men and 1 woman from a private residence in the Diongo neighborhood in Ikiliwindi Mile 10 (Kumba 2, Meme, Sud-Ouest) for an unknown reason.

Looting: Around 12 October 2024 (as reported), Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants looted 2 stores and 16 private residences in Ldubam Goma, department capital Mokolo (Mokolo, Mayo-Tsanaga, Extreme-Nord). The militants also looted small farm animals.
Looting: On 30 August 2022, suspected Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) fighters looted livestock in Moskota (Mayo-Moskota, Mayo-Tsanaga, Extreme-Nord).
On 4 April 2020, military forces attacked the village of Nwa (Donga-Mantung, Nord-Ouest), killing two people and reportedly extorting money and other valuables from the villagers.

On 4 October 2023, Ambazonian Separatists abducted a Government Primary School Teacher at a burial ceremony of his neighbor in Fuanantui (Belo, Boyo, Nord-Ouest). The Separatists accused the teacher of teaching in a government school against the Separatist orders. The Separatists took his identification documents and later released him demanding that he pay money to retrieve his documents.
On 2 June 2021, there was exchange of fire between military forces Ambazonian separatists in Bamunka, Ndop sub-division (Ngo-Ketunjia, Nord-Ouest). There was one casualty as a result of the clash.
On 19 March 2024, a mob of 5 beat and injured a civilian at a funeral ceremony in Dumbo (Misaje, Donga-Mantung, Nord-Ouest) after an argument. There were no fatalities.

On 29 April 2022, over 30 women and children began protesting in front of the North West Governor's Office in Bamenda (Bamenda 1, Mezam, Nord-Ouest) because of a land dispute in Donga Mantung division that have turned violent.

On 6 January 2020, a group of villagers repelled an attack of Ambazonian separatists who attempted to abduct their traditional leader in Babungo village (Ngo-ketunjia, Nord-Ouest). No fatality and/or casualty reported.
On 30 May 2021, the military forces raided Nchum village, Bafut subdivision (Mezam, Nord-Ouest). They shot and killed one civilian, and injured another.

On 17 October 2023, state security forces (coded as military) physically assaulted and injured four civilians transporting ammunition at a vehicular checkpoint along the Kumba - Mamfe road in Konye (Meme, Sud-Ouest). The men, their vehicle, and the ammunition were taken to a detention facility in Konye.
On 18 February 2022, Ambazonian separatists and military forces engaged in an armed clash between Baba I and Babungo (Babessi, Ngo-Ketunjia). There were no reported casualties.

Property destruction: On 17 March 2023, state security forces (coded as military) in Ibal (Bui, Nord-Ouest) fired several gun shots to scare and prevent any unforeseen Ambazonian Separatist attack which damaged the roofs of several civilian homes.
On 12 March 2021, Ambazonian Separatists stabbed a police officer on patrol at Mile 4 Nkwen in Nkwen (Bamenda - Nkwen, Mezam, Nord-Ouest). They made away with his AK47 rifle. No casualties.

On 27 March 2024, Ambazonian Separatists abducted 6 civilians onboard a commercial vehicle at an illegal checkpoint in Sabga (Tubah, Mezam, Nord-Ouest) and took them to their hideout along with the vehicle. The civilians were released the following morning after the Separatists collected their phones and money. The Separatists kept the vehicle and demanded one million Franc CFA from the driver before the release of his vehicle.
On 2 July 2023, ISWAP or Boko Haram militants attacked and killed 2 civilians on their farm in Darak (Darak, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord).
On 1 September 2023, Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants clashed with the military forces in Sandawadjiri (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). Casualties unknown. Weapons and ammunition were stolen.
Looting: On 8 November 2020, Boko Haram nightly looted Modoko village, Koza subdivision (Mayo-Tsanaga, Extreme-Nord), taking away 2 cows and clothes.

On 23 April 2024, security forces, coded as the military forces, clashed with the Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction at a local bar in Owe (Muyuka, Fako, Sud-Ouest). There were no fatalities. No information on the injuries.
On 20 September 2021, Ambazonian separatists attacked a military convoy around Babanki village, Tubah subdivision (Mezam, Nord-Ouest). Casualties unknown.
On 15 November 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected of being ISWAP or Boko Haram militants abducted 8 civilians in Darak (Darak, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord) on two canoes.

On 21 September 2022, Ambazonian Separatists abducted and killed a male civilian in Bombe Konye in Konye subdivision, coded to Konye (Meme, Sud-Ouest) whilst in captivity for allegedly working with government forces in identifying their hideouts.

Property destruction: On 15 July 2021, the Ambazonian separatists Buffalos of Bali Nyonga affiliated with the Ambazonia Restoration Forces burnt the GS Bali school in Bali (Bali, Mezam, Nord-Ouest). The separatists claimed that the Cameroonian military forces (Rapid Intervention) were using the school.
Other: On 13 May 2024, Ambazonian Separatists fired multiple gunshots under unclear circumstances at Mile 4 in Bamenda - Nkwen (Bamenda 3, Mezam, Nord-Ouest).

On 20 December 2023, an IED planted by an unidentified armed group detonated on travelling military and gendarmerie forces along the Mile 24 road, coded to Wum (Wum, Menchum, Nord-Ouest). 3 soldiers and 2 gendarmerie forces were killed.

On 1 October 2021, the Ambazonian flag was hoisted at the Jakiri town Council (Bui, Nord-Ouest). The military forces engaged in fire fights with the separatists as they tried to take it down. There were no fatalities.

Looting: On 29 May 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction forcibly collected, coded as looting, an unspecified amount of money from businessmen and traders at the market square in Beboka (Toko, Ndian, Sud-Ouest).

On 5 July 2021, a group of soldiers allegedly sent by the driver of the Defense Minister severely beat up and arrested one person in Nkolo neighborhood of Yaounde city, Yaounde 1 subdivision (Mfoundi, Centre). The victim was having a private dispute with the Minister's driver.
On 5 April 2021, the military forces engaged in fire fights with Ambazonian separatists in Ndop town (Ngo-Ketunjia, Nord-Ouest). No fatality and/or casualty reported.

Property destruction: On 29 June 2023, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction burned down 3 houses and a provision store belonging to former members of their Separatists faction in Kajifu (Akwaya,Manyu,Sud-Ouest). The former Separatist was accused of joining a new Separatist group that intended to take over control of Akwaya from the ARF factions led by 'General' Ako Giant and 'General' Jonas.

On 13 October 2023, Boko Haram militants [JAS faction] clashed with the military forces at the military outpost in Makoulaye near Kourgui (Mora, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). 4 militants were killed and 3 injured, including a soldier.
Looting: Around 1 August 2024 (as reported), ISWAP or Boko Haram militants looted 2 motorbikes and clothing in Kolofata Guidi (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord).

On 13 August 2022, Ambazonian separatists ambushed the Cameroonian security forces in Magba village (Noun, Ouest) killing a police inspector and a soldier. The separatists also stole their weapons and ammunition.

Movement of forces: Around 7 March 2023, the Cameroonian military forces (Rapid Intervention) were deployed to secure the Bamenda-Mbengwi road, coded to Bamenda (Bamenda 1, Mezam, Nord-Ouest) after the Ambazonian Separatists blocked the road ahead of the senatorial elections.
On 3 April 2021, the military forces shot and killed a civilian in Mbengwi town, Mbeggwi subdivision (Momo, Nord-Ouest), for being the father of an Ambazonian separatist.

Movement of forces: On 13 October 2024, civilians reported the movement of ISWAP or Boko Haram militants in Mbourdas (Mourdas) (Hile-Alifa, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord) and later in the day in Goretal Goutoun (coded separately).

On 10 October 2024, the military forces from the Rapid Intervention ambushed Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants during a security operation in Amchide (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). There were no fatalities. The military forces arrested 2 militants and also recovered rifles, ammunition and military equipment.
Around 6 April 2023, Boko Haram [JAS] militants clashed with the self-defense militia (COVI) in Kerawa (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). 1 militant was killed.

Around 5 December 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed a motorbike taxi driver in Palar neighborhood in Maroua (Maroua 1, Diamare, Extreme-Nord). The victim's throat was slit by the assailants, the reason for the attack is unknown.

Other: On 4 September 2023, around 15 Ambazonian Separatists operatives rounded up civilians and students from the village in the market square in Wum (Menchum, Nord-Ouest), confiscated their phones, and threatened to attack any student or teacher found going to school. The perpetrators ordered civilians to honor the lockdown, returned the victims' phones, and left the area before the arrival of the military.

On 17 November 2022, Ambazonian Separatists invaded a bar in Nkwen (Bamenda - Nkwen, Mezam, Nord-Ouest) owned by a soldier who was present at the time. They tried to seize his rifle, and as he resisted, they ended up shooting and killing him in the bar.

On 22 July 2024, a group of women gathered in Mbessa (Belo, Boyo, Nord-Ouest) in a demonstration against the abduction of a man by the Ambazonian Separatists. The women were marching towards the groups hideout to demand his release when the Separatists opened fire against the group. A women was killed, another person was injured was and several were abducted.

On 22 February 2024, Ambazonian Separatists detonated several road-planted IEDs in Mile 23 Bafut forest, coded to Bafut (Bafut, Mezam, Nord-Ouest). Casualties unknown. No information on the injuries. The Separatists abducted several truck drivers. They were later released when an unspecified amount of money was paid. Several trucks were burnt.

On 10 October 2022, Ambazonian Separatists clashed with military forces in Mamfe (Manyu, Sud-Ouest). The clash happened as the group attacked and killed an unarmed private security guard aiming to raid a back. 1 soldier was injured and the establishment was partially destroyed.
On 14 March 2024, Ambazonian Separatists abducted a civilian along the highway in Mbipgo (Ndu, Donga-Mantung, Nord-Ouest) for an unknown reason.
On 18 October 2020, Ambazonian separatists shot and injured 2 civilians in Bova village, Buea subdivision (Fako, Sud-Ouest), for robbing a chemical store.

On 9 November 2023, a resident mob attacked a thief at the City Chemist Roundabout in Bamenda (Bamenda 1, Mezam, Nord-Ouest) when he tried to steal a bike by stabbing the owner. The security forces intervened and arrested the him.

On 23 May 2023, Ambazonian Separatists clashed with the State security forces, coded as the military forces, stationed around the council building in Ndu (Ndu,Donga-Mantung, Nord-Ouest). Casualties unknown. No information on the injuries. Part of the council building was destroyed.

On 14 May 2023, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction beat and injured a pastor and an unspecified number of Christians when they attacked a church in Mile 14, coded to Buea (Buea, Fako, Sud-Ouest) under unclear circumstances. There were no fatalities.
On 28 March 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants shot and injured 2 civilians along the Mora-Doulo, coded to Mora (Mora, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). The militants looted a motorbike.
On 6 November 2023, Ambazonian Separatists entered the village and abducted a male Fulani in Lassin (Noni, Bui, Nord-Ouest).
On 1 November 2023, the military forces shot and killed a male civilian under unclear circumstances in Kurume (Konye, Meme, Sud-Ouest).
Around 28 September 2024 (as reported), Mbororo militia attacked and killed at least 3 civilians in Sop (Jakiri, Bui, Nord-Ouest) for an unknown reason.
On 9 December 2022, suspected ISWAP or Boko Haram fighters attacked civilians in Tchika (Hile-Alifa, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord). The fighters stole civilian property. Casualties unknown.

On 7 September 2023, Ambazonian Separatists with rifles assaulted and injured a civilian at his residence in Njinikejem, coded to sub-division capital Njinikom (Boyo, Nord-Ouest). The man was the head teacher of a government primary school and the Ambazonian Separatists accused him of cleaning the school premises for school resumption, thereby violating the group's imposed two-week lockdown against the resumption of school.

On 19 August 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a civilian from the field in Ambaram in the commune of Touboro, coded to Touboro (Touboro, Mayo-Rey, Nord). The military forces launched a search operation without any success.
Looting: On 29 September 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants looted 2 motorbikes from civilians in Bia (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord).

On 28 March 2023, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces abducted two oil mill operators in Barombi Mokoko (Ndian, Sud-Ouest). This followed after the Separatists accused the operators of stealing palm nuts from the CDC plantations and processing in their private oil mills. They asked the abductees to pay 300,000 FCFA each.

On 10 April 2024, the military forces clashed with the Ambazonian Separatists in Bamfem, coded to Kumbo (Kumbo, Bui, Nord-Ouest). At least 4, including a suspected Separatists were killed. Their bodies were left near a stream. No information on the injuries.

On 17 December 2023, Ambazonian Separatists attacked military convoy on transit with a road planted IED that partially damaged a military vehicle in Nkarkui (Kumbo, Bui, Nord-Ouest). The military, in retaliation, fired repelling shots that lasted for about an hour until the retreated. Casualties unknown.

On 19 July 2023, state security forces (coded as military) engaged in an armed confrontation with Ambazonian Separatists at their informal vehicular checkpoint in Agyati (Mezam, Nord-Ouest). Two Separatists were killed.

On 31 July 2022, an unidentified armed group members attacked and assaulted 6 aid workers in Buea (Buea, Fako, Sud-Ouest) as the aid workers were unloading a humanitarian truck. The assailants looted their belongings before running off. No fatalities or injuries.

On 21 February 2023, the State forces, coded as the military forces ambushed Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction at a checkpoint in Kombone Mission (Kumba 1, Meme, Sud-Ouest). 1 Separatist and 4 civilians were killed and 6 were injured.

On 26 July 2022, military forces shot and killed 4 male civilians in Diongo in Meme Department, coded to Kumba (Kumba 1, Meme, Sud-Ouest) during a raid against Ambazonia separatists. This operation was after armed fighters' earlier on attacked a military base in the location killing one soldier (coded separately). This led to temporary displacement of civilians.

On 18 January 2021, an unidentified armed group suspected to be Ambazonia separatists and military forces engaged in many localities in Buea (Fako, Sud-Ouest). Shootings were heard in the following quarters: Molyko, Malingo, Santa Barbara, Mile 18, and Bomaka. In most cases, it was claimed that the assailants were confronting military forces. The number of casualties is unknown.

Around 1 May 2020, during a one week raid, the military forces allegedly killed 22 Ambazonian separatists including 2 commanders in attacks on 7 separatists camps in Bafut town, Bamenda subdivision (Mezam, Nord-Ouest). The villagers contest that figure however, saying 13 civilians were killed by the military.

On 7 June 2023, Ambazonian Separatists abducted 3 traders in Watt, Ndu commune, coded to Ndu (Donga-Mantung, Nord-Ouest). The civilians are accused of collaborating with vigilantes to buy stolen goats. No additional information.

On 10 September 2024, Ambazonian Separatists shot, set fire and killed the village chief and his wife in Erat (Mundemba, Ndian, Sud-Ouest) for an unknown reason. The Separatists also burnt the victim's home. The attack and the threats to return from the Separatists caused residents to flee to nearby bushes and to cross the border into Nigeria.

Around 9 April 2024 (as reported), Muslim fishermen armed with shotguns and arrows clashed with ISWAP or Boko Haram militants in Blangoua (Blangoua, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord). 2 were killed and 1 militant was captured. The residents recovered weapons and ammunition. The military forces later arrived to assist the residents.

On 19 October 2024, Ambazonian Separatists abducted a man and his three children from his private vehicle along a road at the Piyin Quarter in Bamenda (Bamenda 3, Mezam, Nord-Ouest). The Separatists forced the man to drive them to an unknown location. The victims were later released after they paid an unspecified amount of money to the Separatists.
Property destruction: Around 24 May 2022, Boko Haram JAS destroyed houses in Sandawadjiri (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord).

On 1 February 2024, traders and loaders clashed with the police forces in Olembe (Ayos, Nyong-et-Mfoumou, Centre) after police forced shopkeepers to leave. The traders also blocked the roads. Casualties unknown. There were several injured.

Around 30 December 2021 (as reported), over 200 recruited workers of the stadium demonstrated in Bafoussam town, Bafoussam 1 subdivision (Mifi, Ouest) after they were not appointed to the due positions.

On 24 October 2020, suspected Ambazonian separatists opened fire on pupils in a private school in Fiango town (Meme, Sud-Ouest), killing 6 children, and injuring 13 others, one of the wounded later died of his wounds (total of 7 fatalities, or 8 according to other sources). The separatists denied having perpetrated that attack and accused the government forces of having done so.
On 29 May 2020, suspected Boko Haram fighters looted three houses in the village of Walaga (Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord), taking away goods and money.

Around 31 July 2020 (as reported), Ambazonian separatists killed at least 15 cows belonging to people of Mbororo community in Konchep village, near Nkambe (Donga-Mantung, Nord-Ouest). This was a retaliation after an Ambazonian fighter was allegedly killed by Mbororos.

On 14 June 2023, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces abducted five civilians from their bars in Badun (Kupe-Manenguba, Sud-Ouest). The abductees were accused of selling Brasseries Brewery products which are banned by the Separatists. No additional information.

On 27 July 2022, members of Wum mobilised with sticks in Wum, Wum subdivision (Menchum, Nord-Ouest) in retaliation to an attack by the Fulani community. Some Wum community members were previously attacked by some Fulani in response to their collaboration with an armed group (likely Ambazonian separatists) in the killing of three Fulani men. Upon arriving at the ceremonial ground, military forces fired several shots in the air to deter the mobilised population who resisted to vacate the area until the arrival of municipal authorities who addressed the crowd. After the address by the municipal authorities, the majority of the population returned home with some setting two houses belonging to Fulani herdsmen ablaze in the neighbourhood of Weindo, Wum. 3 people were killed.

On 31 May 2024, Ambazonian Separatists ambushed and clashed with the security forces, coded as the military forces, along the main road in Baba I (Babessi, Ngo-Ketunjia, Nord-Ouest). There were no fatalities. 1 soldier was injured.

On 8 August 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction clashed with the security forces, coded as the military forces in Big Ngwandi (Konye, Meme, Sud-Ouest). The Separatists detonated an IED that killed 2 soldiers and injured 6 others before clashing with security forces. The casualties on the Separatist side are unknown.
On 28 June 2022, Ambazonian Separatists beheaded a soldier in Konye commune, coded to Konye (Meme, Sud-Ouest). They identified the soldier when he was traveling through public transportation.
Around 11 March 2021 (as reported), Boko Haram fighters killed one person at a location called 'Maison Blanche', 6 kilometers away from Waza village (Logone-Et-Chari, Extreme-Nord).
Looting: On 11 March 2024, suspected ISWAP or Boko Haram militants looted livestock from a grazing area in Ziguague (Waza, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord).
Property destruction: On 13 February 2024, Ambazonian Separatists set fire to a high school facility in Widikum (Widikum, Momo, Nord-Ouest).

Looting: On 25 September 2023, suspected Boko Haram militants [JAS faction] looted a traveling civilian along the Maloumri - Djourou road, coded to Maloumri (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). The militants stole his motorbikes and personal items. The military forces (Rapid Interventions) unsuccessfully searched for the suspects.

On 5 April 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction abducted around 25 civilians in Lissoka (Buea, Fako, Sud-Ouest). The Separatists demanded an unspecified amount for their release.
On 1 January 2024, ISWAP or Boko Haram militants attacked and killed 4 Christians in Fokotol (Fotokol, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord). The militants also abducted 19 civilians during the attack.
Looting: On 5 September 2022, presumed Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) looted Kerawa (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord) stealing 35 livestock and robbed several households.

Looting: On 20 October 2022, Ambazonian Separatists collected an unspecified amount of money from drivers and passengers at a roadblock in Taboh, Upper Bayang commune, coded to Tinto (Manyu, Sud-Ouest). They retreated after the intervention of the military (no information on clashes).
Property destruction: On 16 July 2021, Ambazonian separatists attacked and burnt a military barracks down in Bali-Nyonga town, Batcham subdivision (Bamboutos, Ouest).
Looting: On 18 December 2023, ISWAP or Boko Haram militants looted 2 houses in Waza (Waza, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord).

Around 3 August 2022, the Cameroonian military forces attacked Ngolo Bolo, coded to Konye (Konye, Meme, Sud-Ouest) and killed a civilian and burnt several houses. The military arrested several in Kokkaka village. They were in search for separatists.
On 18 January 2024, military forces, on transit, engaged in a gun exchange with Ambazonian Separatists in Ebendi (Widikum, Momo, Nord-Ouest). No casualties.
Other: On 26 May 2024, the military forces fired several warning shots in Mozogo (Mayo-Moskota, Mayo-Tsanaga, Extreme-Nord) after spotting suspected Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants in the area.
On 17 April 2020, military forces killed a commercial motorcycle rider in Kumba town, Ekondo Titi subdivision (Ndian, Sud-Ouest) during enforcment of counter coronavirus lockdown measures.

Around 28 July 2020 (as reported), the Ambazonian separatists kidnapped and tortured one person around Babessi village (Ngo-Ketunjia, Nord-Ouest). The victim was later released and died of his wounds.

On 6 August 2023, Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants clashed with the military forces in Kolofata (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). The military forces pushed back the militants. The militants stole clothes and food. Casualties unknown.

On 14 August 2023, Boko Haram militants [JAS faction] attacked Kouyape (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). There were no fatalities but 1 civilian was wounded by a knife stabbing. The militants stole from several properties.

On 10 April 2023, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction clashed with the police forces at a checkpoint in Mile 16 in Bolifamba (Buea, Fako, Sud-Ouest). 4 police officers and a commercial bike driver were killed. The Separatists burnt 4 vehicles for violating the Separatists imposed Monday ghost towns.
Other: On 1 July 2024, gendarmerie forces fired sporadic gunshots from the army minor outpost in Fonfukka (Bum, Boyo, Nord-Ouest). The reasons for the gunshots is not known.

On 3 July 2022, members of the Kumba Presbyterian Church protested in Kumba (Ekondo Titi, Ndian, Sud-Ouest) accusing the Reverends of corruption and theft. The security forces (assumed police forces) intervened to disperse them. On 28 August 2022, two of the protesters were arrested by the police in connection to that incident.

Around 2 September 2024 (as reported), Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants attacked and killed 2 civilians aged 50 and 70 years old in Godigong (Mora, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). The militants looted several items.

On 14 August 2024, Ambazonian Separatists detonated a radio-controlled IED on traveling security forces, coded as the military forces on the main road in Bafut (Bafut, Mezam, Nord-Ouest). 2 soldiers were killed and, 2 others were injured. The explosion also damaged a military vehicle.

On 4 February 2024, Ambazonian Separatists stormed a healthcare facility and abducted an unknown number of healthcare workers, including two INGO staff members who were on duty, in Bamali (Ndop, Ngo-Ketunjia, Nord-Ouest).

On 30 September 2022, Ambazonian Separatists tortured a businesswoman in Ntenako (Mamfe, Manyu, Sud-Ouest). She was being extorted an unspecified amount of money and was assaulted and left at her house as the group received information of the arrival of military forces.
Looting: Around 10 May 2023, Boko Haram [JAS] looted a shop in Guidi (Figuil, Mayo-Louti, Nord). Most of the goods were stolen.

On 16 March 2024, police beat Christians in Ngoussou neighborhood in Yaounde (Yaounde 1, Mfoundi, Centre) and arrested 30. They were later released. There were no fatalities. It is suspected that the attack is related to leadership of the Church assembly.

On 2 June 2023, Ambazonian Separatists detonated an IED targeting a state security forces convoy (coded as military) in Bufi (Menchum, Nord-Ouest). The explosion missed the target, but the soldiers stopped and fired gunshots in the area which caused civilians to flee.
Looting: On 6 November 2022, unidentified armed group looted a civilian at a residential area in Kousseri (Kousseri, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord) stealing a motorbike.
Defusal: On 6 December 2021, the military detected and detonated multiple explosives suspected to have been planted by Ambazonian separatists in Wum, Wum (Menchum, Nord-Ouest).

On 6 May 2022, residents of Foumbot demonstrated for the second day against high prices of goods in Foumbot (Foumbot, Noun, Ouest). Demonstrators forced shops to close, beat up some civilians, and destroyed goods.

On 24 October 2024, dozens of women from Mamu protested outside the South West Gendarmerie headquarters Legion in Buea (Buea, Fako, Sud-Ouest), demanding justice for their children and husbands whom the gendarmerie forces arrested late last week. The women say the arrests were unjust and lacked due process. The women called for the immediate release of their husbands and children.
On 16 February 2021, the military forces engaged in fire fights with Ambazonian separatists in Fundong town (Boyo, Nord-Ouest).

Other: On 27 May 2023, state security forces, coded as military forces, shot into the air to scare away Ambazonian Separatists who mounted an informal vehicle checkpoint at Mbot, Nkambe commune, coded to Nkambe (Donga-Mantung Nord-Ouest) in an attempt to attack the Divisional Officer for Ndu. On 21 November 2023, the SOCADEF intercepted and kidnapped more than 6 civilians from three vehicles and a motorcycle along the main road in Konye (Konye, Meme, Sud-Ouest). The also set ablaze the motorcycle.
On 30 October 2020, about 110 Boko Haram fighters reportedly surrendered to the MNJTF forces in Mora town (Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord).

On 18 March 2024, Five Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants beat and injured a civilian in Walassa (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). The militants looted his motorbike.

On 10 July 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction abducted 2 civilians from their private residences in New Town Barombi (Kumba 1, Meme, Sud-Ouest). The Separatists accused the victims of collaborating with the security forces.

On 8 June 2023, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces abducted five drivers and an unknown number of passengers along the Mamfe - Ekok road in Mbakem (Manyu, Sud-Ouest) under unclear circumstances. No additional information.

On 21 February 2024, Ambazonian Separatists restoration forces attacked and killed a civilian in Ikata (Muyuka, Fako, Sud-Ouest), accusing him of leading government forces to the Separatist hideout. On 5 April 2020, two Boko Haram suicide bomber detonated themselves in Amchide village, Kolofata subdivision (Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord), killing themselves, and 7 people, and injuring 15 others. On 30 December 2023, the military forces attacked and killed two Ambazonian Separatists operatives at vehicle checkpoint in Tiben (Batibo, Momo, Nord-Ouest).
On 16 June 2020, military forces reportedly dislodged a separatists camp in Bali town (Mezam, Nord-Ouest), killing 13 fighters and seizing weapons and ammunition.

On 19 November 2020, hundreds of members of the Cameroon association to improve hygiene demonstrated in Kribi town (Ocean, Sud) to mark the World Toilet Day and to call on the authorities to provide more public bathrooms.

Around 24 February 2024 (as reported), ISWAP or Boko Haram militants attacked and injured 1 civilian in Blabine (Blangoua, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord). The militants also vandalized and looted several houses.

Around 3 March 2024 (as reported), Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants attacked and injured a civilian in Lelede neighbourhood behind the hospital in Kolofata (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). The victim was taken to the hospital for treatment.

On 4 September 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction clashed with the security forces, coded as the military forces in Kombone Mission (Kumba 1, Meme, Sud-Ouest). The Pirates requested a ransom of 1.9 billion FCFA, 10 generators, 200 Yamaha horsepower flying boats, and the release of their associates currently held at the Buea Central Prison to release the Divisional Officer of Idabato. On 20 June 2024, Ambazonian Separatists abducted 7 clergymen and 6 parishioners during a church inauguration in Bamali (Ndop, Ngo-Ketunjia, Nord-Ouest). The Separatists accused the church authorities of not informing them about the event. The abductees were released after a ransom was paid.

On 17 July 2023, Ambazonian Separatists shot and killed a man in Mautu (Fako, Sud-Ouest) after accusing him of collaborating with state security forces.

On 23 February 2020, Boko Haram attacked the villages of Tchebetchebe and Dzaba in Mayo Moskota subdivision (Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). They killed one person, and took away foods and goods. Four boys were also shortly held hostages.

On 16 May 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction under General Sagon beat four commercial motorcycle riders at an informal checkpoint in Bamessing (Tubah, Mezam, Nord-Ouest). The separatists took the four motorcycles and their cell phones before releasing them. The riders were accused of defying the one-week lockdown imposed by the Separatists to honor their fallen commander, 'General Sagon'. No further information.

On 11 April 2024, patrolling military forces from the Rapid Intervention clashed with suspected pirates along the Cameroon - Nigeria waterway in Cape Bakassi (Idabato, Ndian, Sud-Ouest). 3 pirates were killed. The military forces arrested 7 men and 3 women.

On 18 July 2024, Ambazonian Separatists abducted a bar owner from his establishment in Mezam neighborhood in Bamenda (Bamenda 3, Mezam, Nord-Ouest). The Separatists accused the civilian of selling Separatist-banned Brasseries Brewery products.

The products from this brewery are banned by the Separatists. The driver and the owner of the products were allowed to leave unharmed.

On 26 December 2022, an Ambazonian Separatist killed a traditional herbalist at Nkuv, coded to Kumbo subdivision (Bui, Nord-Ouest) following an argument over unpaid bills for treatment offered to the separatist on two separate occasions. On 18 July 2024, the security forces, coded as the military forces clashed with the Ambazonian Separatists in an unknown location in the Bali Subdivision (Bali, Mezam, Nord-Ouest). 1 unknown Separatist commander was killed.

On 14 October 2020, Boko Haram attacked Kadje village, around Mora (Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord), killing 2 people.

On 7 April 2024, the military forces clashed and repelled an attack from ISWAP or Boko Haram militants in Fotokol (Fotokol, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord). Casualties unknown. No information on the injuries. The militants looted food items.

On 12 February 2024, Ambazonian Separatists abducted 1 civilian in the Mbelewa neighborhood in Bamenda - Nkwen (Bamenda 3, Mezam, Nord-Ouest). The Separatists demanded 200,000 Franc CFA for his release. The victim had come to visit a friend when he was abducted.

Around 25 March 2024 (as reported), an unidentified armed group hit a commercial bike rider in the left eye with the butt of a rifle in the bush around Mobile neighborhood in Bamenda - Nkwen (Bamenda 3, Mezam, Nord-Ouest) causing him to lose his eye. On 10 September 2023, Ambazonian Separatist from the Restoration Forces ambushed a state security forces patrol (coded as military) in Owe (Fako, Sud-Ouest). No casualties.

Around 11 November 2023, Ambazonian Separatist fighters attacked civilians in Mamfe (Mamfe, Manyu, Sud-Ouest). At least 25 civilians were killed, some victims were burnt alive in their sleep. And some 12 homes were burnt and destroyed.
On 12 April 2020, Boko Haram killed one person in a field near Ashigashiya village, Kolofata subdivision (Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord).

Around 13 May 2024 (as reported), the military forces from the Rapid Intervention clashed with ISWAP or Boko Haram militants in Dabanga (Logone-Birni, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord). Casualties unknown. 300 Nigerian abductees, including 191 children, 99 women and 10 men were liberated. The military forces recovered weapons and ammunition.

On 1 April 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction shot and killed a commercial motorbike rider along a road in Bonakama in Kumba city (Kumba 1, Meme, Sud-Ouest) for disrespecting the Separatists -imposed Monday lockdown.

On 11 January 2021, Boko Haram blocked the road from Kolofata to Gouzoudou village (Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord). They seized one motorbike and destroyed another, and briefly kidnapped two students. No fatality and/or casualty reported.

On 10 July 2024, based on a tip-off, the security forces, coded as the military forces clashed with the Ambazonian Separatists in Betock (Nguti, Kupe-Manenguba, Sud-Ouest). On 4 April 2020, the military forces repelled an attack by Boko Haram on Ndaba IDP camp near Kolofata town (Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord).
Looting: On 25 November 2020, Boko Haram fighters looted Mayo Moskota village (Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord), taking away goods.

On 9 April 2020, military forces tortured and killed a former Ambazonian separatist fighter in Bafia town (Mbam-et-Inoubou, Centre), who had reportedly laid down his arms but not notified authorities.

On 26 January 2023, Ambazonian Separatists from the Buffalos of Bali Nyonga faction abducted some workers of a road construction company (Edge) in Bali commune, coded to Bali (Mezam, Nord-Ouest). They accused their employer of carrying out reconstruction work for the government. The Separatists also took some equipment.

On 20 July 2024, Ambazonian Separatists abducted a civilian from his private residence in Kukaka (Konye, Meme, Sud-Ouest). The Separatists accused him of providing information to the security forces on the Separatist activities.

Looting: On 24 August 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction demanded 500,000 Franc CFA as a fee from a family to organize a funeral ceremony in Mfuni (Mamfe, Manyu, Sud-Ouest). On 27 June 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction detonated 2 IEDs on security forces, coded as the military forces, escorting trucks transporting Brasseries Brewery products along the highway in Ekona Yard (Muyuka, Fako, Sud-Ouest). There were no fatalities or damages to the vehicles.

On 9 June 2020, journalists demonstrated in Douala city (Wouri, Littoral) to demand justice for a journalist reportedly tortured to death by the authorities. The security forces (assumed Police Forces) intervened to disperse the demonstrators.

On 6 October 2023, a mob attacked a man in his late 40's in Bonendale neighborhood in Douala (Douala 1, Wouri, Littoral). There were no fatalities. The Gendarmerie forces intervened. The man was suspected of raping a 12-year-old girl.

On 5 April 2020, Boko Haram ambushed a military patrol on the Sale - Zigague road, in Waza subdivision (Logone-Et-Chari, Extreme-Nord). Two soldiers were killed and arms and ammunition taken away. Other sources say at lest 8 soldiers were killed in that ambush.
On 10 September 2023, Ambazonian Separatists kidnapped a lawyer from Bamenda - Mankon (Mezam, Nord-Ouest). He was released on 13 September 2023 after he paid a ransom.

On 2 January 2024, suspected Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants attacked Djibrili (Mayo-Moskota, Mayo-Tsanaga, Extreme-Nord). There were no fatalities. The militants set fire to houses and abducted 4 civilians. They also stole food and other household items. The next day the security forces conducted a joint search operation of the attackers.
On 31 May 2023, an IED planted by suspected Ambazonian Separatists detonated on patrolling military force (Rapid Intervention) in Mbengwi (Mbengwi, Momo, Nord-Ouest). 5 soldiers were killed.

On 29 June 2021, the MNJTF military ambushed Boko Haram fighters in Mora town (Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord), killing 1 of them and injuring 2 others.
On 2 July 2022, Boko Haram attacked Mada hospital in Makary (Makary, Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord) leading to the death of 1 security guard. A vehicle and motorbike were set on fire.

On 14 November 2023, Ambazonian Separatists kidnapped a vendor from a commercial drinking spot in Ndu (Ndu, Donga-Mantung, Nord-Ouest) on accusations of selling brewery alcoholic drinks to the military against their order.

On 7 May 2022, residents of Foumbot demonstrated for the third day against high prices of goods in Foumbot (Foumbot, Noun, Ouest). Demonstrators forced shops to close, beat up some civilians, and destroyed goods.

Other: On 19 May 2023, Ambazonian Separatists fired warning gunshots in Luh (Donga-Mantung, Nord-Ouest) in order to scare civilians whom they had ordered to stay home.

On 11 August 2024, Ambazonian Separatists from the Restoration Forces faction abducted a woman along the roadside in Kumbe (Konye, Meme, Sud-Ouest). The Separatists accused her of providing information to the military forces.

On 23 August 2024, the military forces clashed with Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants in Goumbouldi, near Igawa Doulo (Mora, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord) during a military operation. 2 militants were killed. On 30 August 2023, Ambazonian Separatists engaged state security forces, coded as military forces, in an armed clash at the forces' position in Tadu (Bui, Nord-Ouest). Casualties are unknown.

On 6 July 2023, Ambazonian Separatists from the SOCADEF faction abducted the community chief from his residence in Ndoi Bakundu (Meme, Sud-Ouest). The victim was accused of collaborating with state security forces and aiding their operations in the region.

Looting: On 16 February 2021, Boko Haram looted several houses in Yegwa village (Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord), taking away clothes.

Around 7 June 2023, Boko Haram (JAS) (likely) militants attacked Amchide (Kolofata, Mayo-Sava, Extreme-Nord) vandalizing shops, stealing cattle and sheep. There were no fatalities. Patrolling military forces (Rapid Intervention) recovered some of the cows.
